Title: AKU-IED Inaugurates Shroff Foundation Learning Resource Centre
NewsSummary: The centre will provide teachers with access to a wide range of resources to support early learning.
NewsContent:
The Aga Khan University Institute for Educational Development (AKU-IED) announced the launch of its refurbished Learning Resource Centre for Early Childhood Education and Development (ECED), through a generous donation from the Shroff Foundation.The centre will provide teachers and their young students with access to a wide range of resources to support early learning.

It features sections dedicated to learning about numeracy, arts, music, physical education, language and science, as well as a comprehensive collection of books (including those hand-made by teachers for their classrooms). It will also be used to train teachers of early years education, introduce them to ready-made learning resources to aid student learning and to give them ideas on how to build low cost, no cost materials to engage young learners.

"This centre will be an excellent resource for teachers and educators, and will help to ensure that our ECED programmes are of the highest quality and offer a hands-on learning experience," said Ms Yasmeen Mehboob, an ECED faculty at AKU-IED.

"We are delighted and honored to partner with the Shroff Foundation to inaugurate our new and improved learning resource centre," said Dr Farid Panjwani, Dean, AKU-IED. "A contribution to education continues to give back even in the long term. And I am confident that continued investment in our future generations will be the solution to many deep-rooted problems in education and in our society."

The centre is located at AKU-IED's campus in Karachi, and will be open to ECED course participants and teachers from the surrounding community.

AKU-IED was established in 1993, with the mission to develop teachers' capacity to teach with progressive pedagogies and student-centred approaches at early childhood, primary and secondary levels, and to enhance the status of the teaching profession in Pakistan and beyond. Today, its 1500+ graduates are improving the performance of schools and education systems by introducing innovative teaching methods and effective leadership practices, inspiring their colleagues and working with parents, communities and government officials.
